correctness.rationale: For n>=5 all four-cycles are hub plus consecutive rim triple and lie in the corresponding five-edge diamond; the spoke-edge properness completes diamond rainbow iff four-cycle rainbow. Each rim edge excludes four distinct spoke colors; the remaining adjacent-rim constraint exactly yields cyclic offset words. A constant offset constructs n-colorings meeting the hub lower bound. The trace counts cyclic offset states bijectively and color-name permutation acts freely. At n=3 the graph K4 has a complete six-edge pair-conflict system; at n=4 the diamond conflict graph is four mutually distinct spokes joined to a rim C4, while adding the rim four-cycle constraint gives eight mutually conflicting edges. Complete direct graph-based checks independently tested small instances. Finite checks are corroboration only; the structural proof is infinite.

originality.rationale: The novel component is the simultaneous exact B/D classification and optimal-coloring count for the infinite wheel family n>=5. The 2026 Wang full text defines D-colorings and gives general degree bounds but no wheel classification; the 2024 planar B paper and 2026 Vuolo full text give broad bounds, not this exact family or trace. Published record for complete multipartite graphs DOES imply D(W4)=6 because W4=K1,2,2; that overlap is explicitly credited and excluded from novelty. Semantic comparisons against B=extended-line-graph coloring, D=diamond-conflict coloring, stronger strong-edge-coloring, and aliases join/fan wheel found no dominating theorem for n>=5. Accessible own historical claims had no B/D-wheel overlap. Nonexhaustive literature coverage and limited publisher access remain risks.

value.rationale: Exact threshold cases and their strict B/D separation in a natural planar hub-cycle family are structurally informative. Beyond a scalar index, the proof classifies every optimal coloring for infinitely many n and gives an explicit finite-matrix exact count growing nontrivially (e.g., normalized counts 1,2,367,11966 for n=5..8). Exact exceptional and label-quotient counts make the result useful for testing rainbow-conflict coloring methods. This is not a mere restatement of the generic degree lower bound: the nontrivial content is the matching sharp construction, D/B equivalence proof and complete enumeration.
